title: Pre-Q4 tracking audit against the documented standards
prompt:
Loam & Ledger (DTC home goods, Shopify, GA4 via GTM, Meta/Google/TikTok/Klaviyo) has engaged you to audit their tracking before Q4 budgets unlock. You are supplied their documented measurement standards, the full list of live campaign links, a summary of the GTM container, and a memo of unexplained symptoms.

Deliver the audit report. For every defect you find: name exactly where it is (which link, tag, trigger, or setting), why it is wrong (against the standards or against correct measurement practice), the measurement or compliance impact — connecting it to the reported symptoms where the evidence supports it — and the concrete fix. Order findings by impact. Close with a short list of what you checked and found clean, so the team knows what they can trust.

Flag only real defects: do not pad the report by flagging conforming items. This is an audit document for internal review; change nothing and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: The audit addresses all supplied artifacts: the campaign links, the GTM/GA4 tag configuration, and the consent setup (a clean-bill mention counts as addressing an artifact).
Each reported defect names its specific location — the exact link/channel, tag, trigger, or setting — precisely enough that an engineer could act without re-deriving the audit.

skill_adherence.check: Flags the uppercase utm_medium=CPC values on the two google-search links as violating the lowercase standard and fragmenting paid-search reporting.
Also flags the google-pmax link's uppercase utm_medium=CPC (the same defect on the Performance Max campaign, not only on the search campaigns).
Flags the klaviyo-welcome link as missing utm_source entirely.
Flags that some Meta links use utm_source=facebook while the standard (and other links) use utm_source=meta, splitting Meta reporting.
Flags the meta-summer link's utm_campaign value ('2026q3 summer sale') for containing spaces / violating the hyphenated campaign format.

Identifies that purchase fires from two live tags (the confirmation-page tag and the place-order button-click tag), double-counting purchases, and connects this to GA4 reporting far more purchases than Shopify.
Identifies that the GA4 purchase tags omit the transaction_id parameter required by the standards, so duplicate purchase events cannot be deduplicated.
Identifies that purchase currency is hardcoded to USD while the ca. storefront transacts in CAD, and connects this to the inflated Canadian revenue.
Identifies that analytics_storage defaults to granted for EEA/UK visitors, violating the documented Consent Mode defaults, and connects this to the legal/privacy finding.
Flags the two http:// newsletter links as violating the https standard and ties them to newsletter traffic landing in Direct (attribution loss on the redirect).
Flags the 'Add to Cart' event name (spaces, not snake_case) as violating the naming standard and explains the add-to-cart reporting going quiet after the rename.
Flags the cart-recovery link carrying utm_campaign twice with different values, and ties it to the cart-recovery campaign appearing under two names.

Identifies that the purchase trigger RegEx ^/order-confirmation also matches /order-confirmation-pending, so purchases fire for unsettled payments, and connects this to the payment-outage / revenue-runs-ahead symptoms.

best_practices.check: No actually conforming item is reported as defective. Examples of clean items are google-brand, begin_checkout, tiktok-prospecting, tiktok-retargeting, pinterest-prospecting, the affiliate links, and the ca-storefront UTMs. Assess the specific parameter against the supplied standard, not the platform label: organic-pinterest has campaign 2026q3-boards, which lacks the required line/goal component, so flagging that naming defect is valid. The organic-instagram source is also absent from the documented source list; identifying that inconsistency is not a false positive. Do not penalize additional evidence-supported findings merely because they lack a separate rubric criterion.
Every reported defect comes with a concrete, implementable fix (what to change, not 'review this').
Findings are ordered or explicitly tiered by measurement/compliance impact, with the purchase-integrity and consent issues ranked above cosmetic UTM issues.
